newsitem.title: USA: De Charette, Christopher seem to get over "snub".
newsitem.headline: De Charette, Christopher seem to get over "snub".

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, said to have snubbed U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher last week, exchanged pleasantries with him at a conference on Monday, U.S. officials said.

In a speech to the conference on aid to Lebanon, the French minister also congratulated Christopher, who retires next month, on his Middle East peacemaking efforts, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Burns' comments suggested the two men wanted to put behind them the alleged snub, in which U.S. officials said De Charette had walked out during a toast in honour of Christopher at a NATO function in Brussels last Tuesday.
De Charette's office said he had not meant to snub Christopher. A senior French official said the tribute to the secretary of state had not been on the agenda at the NATO gathering.

"The secretary was seated with Minister De Charette at the conference. He greeted him. They didn't have a bilateral meeting but they saw each other and they had a chance to exchange pleasantries as you would expect," Burns said of Monday's meeting at the State Department.

"Minister de Charette said at the top of his intervention that the secretary was a very active and creative presence in the Middle East and he congratulated the secretary for that. Of course, we agree with Minister de Charette. Nice to hear those kind of words, very nice indeed," Burns added.

Reporters were allowed in for Christopher's opening speech to the meeting. De Charette, although seated at a side of the table facing away from the podium, was one of the few to turn around to listen. Reporters were then ushered out.
The alleged snub in Brussels followed a series of disputes between Paris and Washington including over the question of who will hold NATO's southern command, based in Naples.

At a ceremony in Paris last month, de Charette gave Christopher a retirement gift of French novels. Some diplomats said it was a back-handed compliment as the novels were all in French, in which Christopher is not known to be fluent.
